newsitem.title: THAILAND: SOCCER-THAIS RAVE OVER MANCHESTER UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THAIS RAVE OVER MANCHESTER UNITED.

text.p: Manchester United may have been fortunate to beat Thailand 2-0 in a friendly on Thursday but for many in the 25,000-strong crowd it was not the score that mattered.
United mania has hit Thailand. Since about 1,000 fans mobbed the team on its arrival at the airport in the early hours of Wednesday morning the squad have been treated like visiting pop stars.

United's downtown hotel has been booked out by local fans anxious to stay close to the stars, crowds of 4,000 people have paid to watch and cheer United's training sessions and the team's coach has been chased around town.

"I love Manchester, especially Roy Keane and Nicky Butt, they are the best," said 19-year-old Kusana Ongsaarn of Bangkok, one of about 3,000 fans who stayed after the match to watch the team coach leave.

In a nation where the Manchester United club magazine sells some 18,000 copies a month, even junior squad members have been treated like celebrities. Rarely can the team have played in such a home from home.
The crowd, dressed mostly in red with many sporting the team's colours, clapped and applauded the United corners, throw-ins and goals.
Females comprised a substantial part of a crowd which screamed and cheered the United substitutes as they warmed up on the stadium's running track during the game.
The stadium public address system played "Glory,Glory Man United" as the players walked off the field with fireworks thundering overhead.
Some of the 400 paramilitary assisting regular police with crowd control pressed United players for autographs.
United Manager Alex Ferguson, overawed by the team's welcome on Wednesday, was full of praise for the reception they have received in Thailand and promised to return in two years' time.

"It's part of being Manchester United but it is kind of wonderful in its way. We are clearly delighted with the reception we have had here from so many young people," he told reporters after the game.

Possibly because of a half-paced United performance, which could have seen them beaten by a Thai team which squandered several clear chances, Ferguson said there were no plans to let the squad mingle with fans after Thursday's game.
Although four members of United's non-playing entourage were seen sampling Bangkok's nightlife on Thursday night, the squad were scheduled to take an early Friday morning flight to Hong Kong.
